Without `-m`, `git read-tree <tree1> <tree2>` reads both trees into stage 0; it only fails if they share a path, and a checkpoint's tracked tree and its untracked-files parent never do. Repro on git 2.43: read-tree of a tree with `a.ts` and a tree with `new.ts` gives `100644 ... 0 a.ts` and `100644 ... 0 new.ts`, and `write-tree` succeeds. The path is also covered by `sidecar/session-changes.test.ts`, whose checkpoints carry an untracked third parent (including an agent-created `new.ts`), and by a manual run where agent-created untracked files showed up in Last turn and Session.

discussion_comments.comment_body:
Valid, fixed in e4b6ea149d.

A polling start line is now dropped only when its own successful end follows it. Starts and ends are paired in order, by command, request ID and client ID, because some clients reuse request IDs (for example `hub-client-1`). As a result:

- A poll that never finished keeps its start line, so a hub that stopped answering still shows up in the report.
- A failed poll keeps both its start and its end.

Added a test for a start with no end, and tightened the existing test to check that a failed poll keeps both lines.

Fixed in 202642e: parseStatus now keeps the original path on R/C records (originalPath on the file entry). The webview includes it in unstage actions (unstagePaths helper, used for row, group, and breadcrumb unstage) and passes it to get_git_file_diff so a staged rename reads HEAD at the old path. Covered by a real-repo test that git mv's a file, checks the diff shows the old contents, unstages both paths, and verifies the old path is no longer staged as a deletion.
Fixed in 202642e: numstat records split on the first two tabs only and the remainder is kept as the filename, with a test for a tab-containing name.

Valid, fixed. A link whose target is a directory already on the current copy chain, or an ancestor of one (`.`, `..`, a sibling that links back), is now skipped and listed in `skippedPaths` instead of being expanded again, and the number of linked-directory expansions is capped (`MAX_LINK_EXPANSIONS`). Covered by "skips links that loop back into a directory being copied": twenty links to `.` plus one to `..` finish in well under a second with only the real content copied.

Fixed. An entry whose value is an inline scalar, like `disabled: true` or `disabled: false # note`, is now a single line, so an indented comment after it stays with the author. Block scalars (`|`, `>`) and nested values still take their indented continuation lines with them. Test added for both disabling and re-enabling.

Valid, and it exposed the real problem: the extension kept its own copy of the SDK's rules for reading a rule's enabled state, and this was the fourth case where the copy disagreed with the SDK. The copy is gone. The Rules panel, both write paths, and the editor now call `parseRuleConfigFromMarkdown` / `parseSkillConfigFromMarkdown` from `@cline/core`, so they cannot disagree with what the SDK loads. A file with non-mapping frontmatter (which the SDK loads as having no metadata) is disabled by adding a `disabled: true` block above it, and re-enabling restores it exactly; a comment-only block gets the flag appended inside it. Tests cover both, plus a scratch property check of ~16k generated shapes against the SDK parser as the oracle with zero refusals of loadable files. A file the SDK does not load at all now shows as off, since nothing from it reaches the model.

Fair point. Switched to splitting on `path.sep` only (same approach as the SDK's workspace file-indexer), so POSIX filenames containing a literal backslash are left intact. Added a POSIX-only test for that case.
